ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a galvanic cell with a Cu strip in CuNO3(aq) on the left and a Zn strip in Zn(NO3)2(aq) on the right, connected by an external wire and a NaBr salt bridge. The reaction printed below the diagram is 2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) -> 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq), with E° = +1.28 V. Reasoning: For the shown spontaneous reaction, the aqueous species in the reaction quotient are Cu+ and Zn2+; the solids Zn(s) and Cu(s) are omitted. Thus Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu+]^2. As the reaction proceeds forward, Zn(s) is oxidized to Zn2+, so [Zn2+] increases, while Cu+ is reduced to Cu(s), so [Cu+] decreases. Both changes make Q increase. By the Nernst equation, Ecell = E°cell - (RT/nF) ln Q, so an increasing Q lowers the cell voltage. Therefore, the overall voltage decreases as the reaction progresses, specifically as [Zn2+] increases.
